Information provided by GLOS supports the regional marine economy, improves forecasts, and supports decision-making and nearshore safety for countless stakeholders. Cutting or reducing funding would have wide-ranging impacts on Great Lakes communities’ economies and safety.

Look at all of this amazing, comprehensive, real-time, FREE data that GLOS platforms in the Great Lakes. If that goes away, it either won't be replaced or you'll have to pay to access it. glos.org/priorities/s...

Michigan is central to four of the five Great Lakes, giving Michiganders a special connection to the waters. GLOS supports a wide network of partners who maintain the lakes’ observing system, which provides data to tens of thousands throughout the 'Great Lakes State' on seagull.glos.org.

Hundreds of thousands of Ohioans drink water drawn from Lake Erie. IOOS funding, managed regionally via GLOS, supports operations of the observing network and data sharing via GLOS' Seagull. This includes sensors on the lakes and throughout the watershed. Find your data at seagull.glos.org

The Great Lakes has seen an increase in both winter-only and, more importantly, year-round observing platforms over the past couple of years. GLOS expects these platforms to be reporting data on Seagull this winter: glos.org/2025-26-wint...

The Great Lakes Observing System (GLOS) is integral to supporting Great Lakes communities to safeguard residents and local economies, but administrative delays at OMB are putting GLOS funding at risk.

Demand for real-time Great Lakes data is growing, while federal funding remains uncertain. Your yearend gift helps keep the buoy network online & supports new technology to benefit the region.

Illinois and Indiana are closely connected to the great Lake Michigan. GLOS plays a vital role in the observing network of partners that helps ensure it remains safe for drinking, swimming, and fishing. GLOS facilitates data sharing from assets operated by various collaborators & partners on Seagull
